newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Investors pile into Portugal's Inparsa rights.
newsitem.headline: Investors pile into Portugal's Inparsa rights.

text.p: Buoyed by optimism about the future of the wood-to-media group Inparsa, former Sonae Investimentos concerns that are being spun off, investors were buying up the rights heavily to the new holding on Friday, the penultimate day of the offer.

The rights were up 16 escudos at 650 in trade of 1.83 million. Two rights buy one share in Inparsa, which groups Sonae Industria and Pargeste, whose interests range from construction through tourism to media.
Some investors had clearly opted to sell their Sonae Industria and buy the rights to Inparsa as the wood concern had lost since the launch of the rights offer on February 17.
But it was recovering some of the ground on Friday, gaining 4.2 percent at 1,500 escudos.
"Many investors believe in the businesses that are in Pargeste and buy Inparsa", said one share trader.

But it was also possible that Figest, the personal holding of Belmiro de Azevedo, chairman of both Sonae Investimentos and Inparsa, had been boosting its stake in the new holding from the 52.1 percent it would receive under the terms of the split.
Traders said that non-residents had been sellers of the rights.
According to some analysts, the theoretical equilibrium price of Inparsa would be 1,400 escudos per share, or 720 escudos for each of the rights.
Since trade in the rights was launched, 4.99 million have changed hands in trade worth 3.1 billion escudos at prices ranging between a high of 670 and a low of 524.

A study by Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) forecast that Inparsa should make a net profit of 1.25 billion escudos in 1997 on sales of 108.1 billion and 2.24 billion next year on turnover of 121.3 billion.
"The growth in profit in Inparsa...is pretty dependent on Sonae Industria which should show (profit) growth from 639 million escudos in 1997 to 1.76 billion in 1998," said an analyst at the bank.
Pargeste profit is seen rising 33 percent over the period to 1.13 billion.

BPI calculated the net asset value (NAV) of Inparsa at 37.8 billion and if the stock traded at a discount of 30 to 40 percent to that value, this would point to a share price of between 1,150 and 1,350 escudos.
Inparsa, which controls 62 percent of Sonae Industria and 100 percent of Pargeste, is expected to be admitted to trade on the Lisbon bourse around the end of March.
